criterion_or_note: Nursing Levels of Care
Handwritten numbers above level columns

These guidelines are meant to provide parameters for standardization. Multiple line items can increase the level of care depending on the nursing interventions required as 
well as state regulation criteria. Documentation is a critical component. Complete Oct 30, 2020 /Modified 5/24/21/ Modified 5/25/23 / Modified 7/15/2024
Healthy infant >35 weeks gestation
Babies who require routine evaluation and management of lab testing; glucose, bilirubin
Babies who demonstrate prolonged transition after birth, requiring short term O2 therapy, monitored by pulse ox, who are able to be weaned to RA within the first 4-6 hours of life
Babies who have NAS and need observation, but who are stable and do not require treatment
Anti-infective and asymptomatic
Babies being treated for seizure disorder that are stable
Babies requiring continuous phototherapy after mother's discharge
Babies requiring continuous servo controlled environment for thermoregulation
Babies requiring evaluation and treatment for suspected sepsis
Babies requiring gavage feeds
Babies requiring supplemental respiratory support including short term CPAP or mechanical ventilation for less than 24 hours
Babies requiring supplemental respiratory support of O2 therapy for <= 30 days FIO2 >21% to < 40% via hood, nasal cannula or <=1L/min HFNC
Babies who demonstrate prolonged transition after birth, requiring short term O2 therapy, monitored by pulse ox, who are unable to be weaned to RA within the first 4 hours of life
Babies with neonatal abstinence syndrome requiring treatment
Feed and Grow
Infants > 32 weeks or weigh > 1500 grams who do not have specific medical needs that meet level III criteria
IV therapy, TPN once maintenance is established
Short term central lines UAC, UVC, PICC (discuss with facility NICU medical director for parameters <3, 5, 7 days)
Anti-infective and SYMPTOMATIC (hypotonia, tachypnea, tachycardia, temperature instability)
Babies requiring arterial catheterization for frequent ABG analysis or monitoring (hemodynamically stable)
Babies requiring red blood cell transfusion - blood product transfusion
Babies requiring supplemental respiratory support of O2 therapy greater than or equal to 40%, NIPPV or mechanical ventilation or HFNC >1L/min
Babies with acute cardiac instability, including acute CHF or unstable cardiac arrhythmia to include cardioversion
Babies with birth asphyxia or 5 minute apgar of 6 or less
Cerebral Spinal Fluid (CSF) drainage with documented hydrocephalus
Complex Medical Condition - Stable
External Ventricular drain (EVD - neurosurgery)
Exchange transfusion, partial
Infant requiring sustained life support
Long term central lines UAC, UVC, PICC (discuss with facility NICU Medical Director for parameters > 3, 5, 7, 14 days)
Peritoneal dialysis
Surgical Repair of Stable Conditions
TPN while adjusting towards maintenance, IVF Resuscitation, volume expanders
ECMO / ECLS
Exchange transfusion. Double volume (falls under hyperbilirubinemia - see tab below)

Hemodynamically unstable or highly likely to become hemodynamically unstable due to oxygenation and perfusion insufficiencies requiring frequent nurse interventions every 15 minutes 
including, but not limited to, multiple invasive lines, multiple vasopressor titrations, and fluid and/or blood resuscitation, Hemodynamic monitoring including arterial line, ICP Monitoring, 
Continuous EEG Monitoring
<= 72 hours
High Frequency Ventilation
Hemodialysis
Mechanical Ventilation and respiratory interventions every 1-2 hours (excluding weaning) FIO2> 50% or Oxygen Index > 15 or PEEP >8
Nitric Oxide
Prostaglandin for PDA Patency
Regional transport center unstable incoming or outgoing neonatal transports
Surgical repair of unstable complex conditions
